disease_symptoms.s3: milky to amber-colored bacterial droplet exudate on blighted bark and fruit under humid conditions.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Overwinters in canker margins on twigs and trunks
disease_causes.c2: In spring, oozing bacteria are carried by rain splash, bees, and flies to open blossoms
disease_causes.c3: Pathogen travels downward through phloem and xylem into branches.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune blighted twigs in dry winter weather 20-30 cm below visible lesion, dipping tools in 70% alcohol or 10% bleach between every cut
disease_prevention.p2: Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers that stimulate soft succulent shoots.
disease_prevention.p3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced N-P-K plant nutrition tailored to crop stage; avoid excessive nitrogen.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply Potassium (K) (Sulfate of Potash) to reinforce plant vascular tissue and cell wall rigidity.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Apply bio-bactericides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Pseudomonas fluorescens during bloom. Streptomycin sulfate or kasugamycin sprays during flowering risk periods. Fixed copper sprays applied at silver-tip bud break.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Mancozeb (0.2%) or Chlorothalonil contact protectant before anticipated wet weather.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole systemic treatment where permitted.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf4: Soil drench with bio-inoculant Trichoderma harzianum or Streptomyces lydicus.

organic_remedies.org1: Apply bio-bactericides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Pseudomonas fluorescens during bloom. Streptomycin sulfate or kasugamycin sprays during flowering risk periods. Fixed copper sprays applied at silver-tip bud break.
organic_remedies.org2: Koppert Veni GoKlean / Bacillus subtilis bio-protection foliar spray.
organic_remedies.org3: Cold-pressed Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or horticultural botanical oil.
organic_remedies.org4: Potassium bicarbonate spray (5 g/L) to alter leaf surface pH and suppress pathogens.

disease_control.dc1: Prune out and immediately incinerate or bury visibly infected tissues.
disease_control.dc2: Sterilize all pruning shears, knives, and equipment with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
disease_control.dc3: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; irrigate strictly at the root zone via drip lines.
disease_control.dc4: Apply targeted bio-fungicide or bactericide at earliest detection of initial symptoms.

disease_symptoms.s1: Rough, abnormal, tumor-like swellings (galls) on roots, crown (ground level), and woody lower stems

disease_symptoms.s3: older galls turn hard, woody, dark brown, and fissured.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_symptoms.s2: Infected tissues disintegrate into a soft, mushy, slimy liquefaction accompanied by a foul, putrid odor caused by secondary rotting bacteria.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c2: Enters through harvest wounds, insect bites, freeze damage, or lenticels under anaerobic waterlogging.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Harvest during dry weather

disease_symptoms.s2: Infected tissues disintegrate into a soft, mushy, slimy liquefaction accompanied by a foul, putrid odor caused by secondary rotting bacteria.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Pathogen produces copious pectolytic enzymes (pectin lyase, polygalacturonase) that dissolve the middle lamella of host plant cells
disease_causes.c2: Enters through harvest wounds, insect bites, freeze damage, or lenticels under anaerobic waterlogging.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Harvest during dry weather
disease_prevention.p2: Avoid bruising and mechanical abrasion of tubers/roots
disease_prevention.p3: Cure tubers before storage (promote suberization)
disease_prevention.p4: Ensure well-ventilated, cold storage conditions (4°C for potatoes).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced N-P-K plant nutrition tailored to crop stage; avoid excessive nitrogen.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply Potassium (K) (Sulfate of Potash) to reinforce plant vascular tissue and cell wall rigidity.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Post-harvest wash with chlorinated water (50-100 ppm free chlorine). Biocontrol with Pseudomonas fluorescens or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens dip. Dust seed pieces with mancozeb.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Mancozeb (0.2%) or Chlorothalonil contact protectant before anticipated wet weather.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole systemic treatment where permitted.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf4: Soil drench with bio-inoculant Trichoderma harzianum or Streptomyces lydicus.

organic_remedies.org1: Post-harvest wash with chlorinated water (50-100 ppm free chlorine). Biocontrol with Pseudomonas fluorescens or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens dip. Dust seed pieces with mancozeb.
organic_remedies.org2: Koppert Veni GoKlean / Bacillus subtilis bio-protection foliar spray.
organic_remedies.org3: Cold-pressed Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or horticultural botanical oil.
organic_remedies.org4: Potassium bicarbonate spray (5 g/L) to alter leaf surface pH and suppress pathogens.

disease_control.dc1: Prune out and immediately incinerate or bury visibly infected tissues.
disease_control.dc2: Sterilize all pruning shears, knives, and equipment with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
disease_control.dc3: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; irrigate strictly at the root zone via drip lines.
disease_control.dc4: Apply targeted bio-fungicide or bactericide at earliest detection of initial symptoms.

disease_symptoms.s1: Superficial, raised, or deeply pitted rough corky brown lesions on the skin of developing tubers
disease_symptoms.s2: Lesions may coalesce to cover substantial portions of the tuber surface, severely reducing commercial quality.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Soil-dwelling filamentous actinomycete that penetrates young tubers through immature lenticels and stomata
disease_causes.c2: Produces thaxtomin phytotoxins that disrupt plant cellulose synthesis.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain soil pH below 5.2 (scab bacteria are suppressed in acidic soils)
disease_prevention.p2: Keep soil moisture high (near field capacity) during the 4-6 weeks of tuber initiation
disease_prevention.p3: Rotate with alfalfa, rye, or corn.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

Mango___Anthracnose.scientific_name: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides / Colletotrichum acutatum / Colletotrichum lindemuthianum

disease_symptoms.s1: Dark brown to black sunken circular necrotic lesions on foliage, stems, flowers, and fruit
disease_symptoms.s2: Under moist humid conditions, concentric salmon-pink or orange gelatinous spore masses (acervuli) erupt in lesion centers.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Survives as dormant mycelium or appressoria on plant debris, seed coats, or infected twigs
disease_causes.c2: Conidia are spread by splashing raindrops and wind-driven mist
disease_causes.c3: Fungi penetrate cuticle directly via specialized melanized appressoria.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Use certified disease-free seeds
disease_prevention.p2: Prune dense canopies to promote rapid drying of foliage
disease_prevention.p3: Remove fallen leaves and mummified fruits
disease_prevention.p4: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf4: Soil drench with bio-inoculant Trichoderma harzianum or Streptomyces lydicus.

Plums___Black_Knot.plant_name: Plums (Plums, prunes, tart cherries, sweet cher)

disease_symptoms.s1: Elongated, rough, velvety olive-green swellings on twigs and branches that expand over 1-2 years into hard, coal-black, cracked, brittle, knotty galls that encircle and girdle branches.
disease_symptoms.s2: Stunted vegetative growth and reduced photosynthetic vigor.
disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Ascospores mature in pseudothecia on 2-year-old knots during spring rainy periods and infect succulent green shoots
disease_causes.c2: The fungus stimulates abnormal cell division in xylem and bark parenchymatous tissue.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune out galls during dormant season, cutting at least 10-15 cm below the visible knot margin
disease_prevention.p2: Destroy or burn prunings immediately
disease_prevention.p3: Eradicate wild cherry and plum trees near commercial orchards.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply Potassium (K) (Sulfate of Potash) to reinforce plant vascular tissue and cell wall rigidity.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole systemic treatment where permitted.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf4: Soil drench with bio-inoculant Trichoderma harzianum or Streptomyces lydicus.

Potato___Late_Blight_of_Potato_and_Tomat.disease_name: Late Blight of Potato and Tomato

disease_symptoms.s1: Water-soaked, pale-to-dark green irregular spots on leaves and stems, turning dark purplish-brown with pale green margins
disease_symptoms.s2: In cool, wet weather, a delicate white fuzzy mildew appears on the lower leaf surface
disease_symptoms.s3: Infected tubers develop irregular reddish-brown granular dry rot.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Historic cause of the 1845 Irish Potato Famine
disease_causes.c2: Overwinters as mycelium in infected seed tubers, volunteer potatoes, or cull piles
disease_causes.c3: Biflagellate zoospores emerge from sporangia in free water and infect plants rapidly within hours.

disease_symptoms.s1: Severe swelling, spindle-shaped club-like distortion, and gall formation on main taproots and lateral roots
disease_symptoms.s2: Above ground: pale yellow foliage, mid-day wilting on warm sunny days, and severe plant stunting.

disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Soil-borne obligate parasite
disease_causes.c2: Resting spores persist in soil for up to 15-20 years
disease_causes.c3: In wet soil, biflagellate primary zoospores hatch, infect root hairs, and stimulate host cells to divide (hyperplasia) and enlarge (hypertrophy).
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p2: Improve field drainage

disease_prevention.p4: Clean tractor tires.

disease_causes.c2: Ejected ascospores infect open grass flowers during damp bloom periods.

disease_prevention.p1: Use certified ergot-free seed

disease_prevention.p4: Mow roadside grasses before blooming.

Banana___Fusarium_Wilt__including_Panama.scientific_name: Fusarium oxysporum (e.g. f. sp. cubense, lycopersici, vasinfectum)

disease_symptoms.s1: Unilateral (one-sided) yellowing of leaves
disease_symptoms.s2: leaf buckling and wilting from bottom upwards
disease_symptoms.s3: distinct dark red-brown to chocolate vascular ring discoloration in xylem vessels
disease_symptoms.s4: stunted growth and death.

disease_causes.c1: Soil-borne pathogen producing thick-walled chlamydospores that endure in soil for 20-30+ years
disease_causes.c2: Enters root hairs, colonizes xylem, and releases fusaric acid, causing vascular collapse.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Fusarium-resistant tomato hybrids, Tropical Race 4 quarantine for banana)
disease_prevention.p2: Strictly disinfect farm machinery and boots
disease_prevention.p3: Solarize soil with plastic sheets.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply Potassium (K) (Sulfate of Potash) to reinforce plant vascular tissue and cell wall rigidity.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

Peach___Peach_Leaf_Curl___Leaf_Blister.scientific_name: Taphrina deformans (peach leaf curl) / Taphrina caerulescens (oak leaf blister)

disease_symptoms.s1: In spring, emerging leaves become thickened, puckered, twisted, and severely distorted
disease_symptoms.s2: color shifts from normal green to reddish, purplish, or chlorotic yellow
disease_symptoms.s3: leaves develop a velvety gray-white sheen of naked asci before turning brown and dropping.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Ascospores and blastoconidia (yeast-like budding spores) overwinter on bark, branch twigs, and bud scales
disease_causes.c2: In cool wet spring weather, rain washes spores into swelling buds, where mycelium invades succulent leaf tissues.
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant curl-resistant cultivars (e.g., 'Frost', 'Avalon', 'Muir')
disease_prevention.p2: Prune infected twigs after premature defoliation and boost tree vigor with nitrogen fertilizer and irrigation.
disease_prevention.p3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.

disease_symptoms.s3: Premature leaf chlorosis, yellowing, and leaf drop.
disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Overwinters in pseudothecia on dead fallen leaf litter
disease_causes.c2: In spring rain, shooting ascospores infect expanding blossom clusters and young leaves
disease_causes.c3: Secondary cycles propagate via conidia (Spilocaea pomi) all season long.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Shred fallen autumn leaves with a flail mower or apply 5% urea spray to hasten leaf decomposition
disease_prevention.p2: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., 'Prima', 'Liberty', 'Freedom', 'GoldRush').
disease_prevention.p3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_prevention.p4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced N-P-K plant nutrition tailored to crop stage; avoid excessive nitrogen.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply Potassium (K) (Sulfate of Potash) to reinforce plant vascular tissue and cell wall rigidity.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Supplement with soluble Calcium (Calcium Nitrate) and Silicon to thicken leaf epidermal barriers.
fertilizer_recommendation.f4: Incorporate well-decomposed organic compost to enrich beneficial soil microbial antagonists.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Koppert biological products: Veni GoKlean
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Mancozeb (0.2%) or Chlorothalonil contact protectant before anticipated wet weather.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole systemic treatment where permitted.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf4: Soil drench with bio-inoculant Trichoderma harzianum or Streptomyces lydicus.

organic_remedies.org1: Koppert biological products: Veni GoKlean
organic_remedies.org4: Potassium bicarbonate spray (5 g/L) to alter leaf surface pH and suppress pathogens.

disease_control.dc1: Prune out and immediately incinerate or bury visibly infected tissues.
disease_control.dc2: Sterilize all pruning shears, knives, and equipment with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
disease_control.dc3: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; irrigate strictly at the root zone via drip lines.
disease_control.dc4: Apply targeted bio-fungicide or bactericide at earliest detection of initial symptoms.

disease_symptoms.s1: Bleached, matted, straw-colored circular patches (20-60 cm) appearing upon winter snowmelt

disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p1: Avoid late-autumn applications of high-nitrogen fertilizer that promote lush succulent growth
disease_prevention.p2: Mow grass late into autumn
disease_prevention.p3: Aerate compacted turf
disease_prevention.p4: Install snow fencing to avoid heavy drifts.

disease_symptoms.s4: Blemishes, corky scars, or rots on harvested plant organs and fruit.

disease_causes.c2: CMV and Potyviruses are stylet-borne non-persistently by aphids (Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae).
disease_causes.c3: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.
disease_causes.c4: Maintain field sanitation and crop health.

disease_prevention.p2: Wash hands with soap before touching plants
disease_prevention.p3: Eliminate aphid weed reservoirs
disease_prevention.p4: Use certified virus-free seed.

disease_prevention.p3: Soil solarization with plastic sheeting
disease_prevention.p4: Deep summer plowing.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Koppert beneficial nematodes (Steinernema feltiae for pest control) or bionematicides: Paecilomyces lilacinus (Purpureocillium lilacinum)

organic_remedies.org1: Koppert beneficial nematodes (Steinernema feltiae for pest control) or bionematicides: Paecilomyces lilacinus (Purpureocillium lilacinum)
organic_remedies.org4: Potassium bicarbonate spray (5 g/L) to alter leaf surface pH and suppress pathogens.

disease_control.dc1: Prune out and immediately incinerate or bury visibly infected tissues.
disease_control.dc2: Sterilize all pruning shears, knives, and equipment with 70% isopropyl alcohol.

disease_control.dc4: Apply targeted bio-fungicide or bactericide at earliest detection of initial symptoms.

disease_symptoms.s1: Crisp, slender green pods with uniform color and smooth epidermal surface.
disease_symptoms.s2: Vibrant trifoliate green leaves with no chlorosis, mosaic, or rust pustules.
disease_symptoms.s3: Vigorous upright or climbing vine habit with healthy white/purple blossoms.

disease_causes.c1: Well-aerated loamy soil with active Rhizobium nitrogen-fixing root nodules and balanced moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-legume crops to keep soil-borne pathogens in check.
disease_prevention.p2: Water at soil level early in the morning to prevent damp leaves and fungal spore germination.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Low-nitrogen, high-phosphorus organic fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10 or 3-12-12).
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Beans fix their own atmospheric nitrogen via symbiotic bacteria; avoid excess synthetic nitrogen which causes lush foliage with few pods.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention required for healthy legumes.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Preventative neem oil or insecticidal soap if early aphid scouts appear.

organic_remedies.org1: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium leguminosarum at sowing to boost root nodule development.
organic_remedies.org2: Mulch with clean straw to preserve soil moisture and regulate root temperature.

disease_control.ctrl1: Provide sturdy trellising for pole varieties to ensure maximum air circulation.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, firm deep-purple fruits with fresh bright green calyx and unblemished skin.
disease_symptoms.s2: Broad velvety green foliage free of flea beetle holes, little leaf phyllody, or wilt symptoms.
disease_symptoms.s3: Sturdy central stem supporting continuous violet star-shaped flowers and developing fruit.

disease_causes.c1: Warm full-sun climate (24-32°C), nutrient-rich fertile organic soil, and steady moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain warm root temperature and avoid waterlogging to prevent root rot complexes.
disease_prevention.p2: Install yellow sticky traps to intercept whiteflies, jassids, and leafhoppers early.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced organic fertilizer (NPK 10-10-10 or 8-16-16) with supplemental Calcium and Magnesium.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Side-dress with well-decomposed cow manure or vermicompost every 3 weeks during active fruiting.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No pesticides needed for vigorous healthy plants.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) spray if fruit and shoot borer caterpillars are scouted in the area.

organic_remedies.org1: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) foliar spray every 10 days as a natural repellent.
organic_remedies.org2: Companion planting with coriander and marigold to attract beneficial hoverflies and predatory wasps.

disease_control.ctrl1: Stake heavy fruiting branches to keep purple eggplants off damp soil surfaces.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, uniform dark green cylindrical fruits with crisp texture and fresh bloom.
disease_symptoms.s2: Broad triangular leaves with vibrant chlorophyll and zero powdery or downy mildew patches.
disease_symptoms.s3: Active climbing tendrils and plentiful bright yellow blossoms with strong bee pollination.

disease_causes.c1: Consistent deep watering, full sunshine, and fertile organic soil enriched with compost.

disease_prevention.p1: Grow on vertical trellises or A-frames to keep foliage dry and promote rapid air circulation.
disease_prevention.p2: Drip irrigate at the base; avoid overhead sprinkling that triggers downy mildew.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium organic fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10) with seaweed meal for trace minerals.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with vermicompost when flowering begins.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical fungicides necessary for healthy cucurbits.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Preventative copper or sulfur spray only if persistent humid rain occurs.

organic_remedies.org1: Milk spray dilution (40% milk / 60% water) weekly to create a protective bio-film against mildews.
organic_remedies.org2: Encourage pollinator bees by planting dill and borage nearby.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest cucumbers regularly when crisp and tender to stimulate continued floral production.

disease_symptoms.s1: Crisp, brightly colored orange taproot with smooth skin and sweet crisp internal core.
disease_symptoms.s2: Lush, feathery fern-like green foliage with zero leaf blight lesions or yellowing.
disease_symptoms.s3: Firm root shoulder protected beneath the soil line to avoid greening from sunlight.

disease_causes.c1: Loose, stone-free sandy loam soil with consistent moisture and mild cool-season temperatures.

disease_prevention.p1: Thin seedlings to 2-3 inches apart to ensure uniform root development without crowding.
disease_prevention.p2: Hilling soil over root shoulders to prevent bitter green chlorophyll development.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Low-nitrogen, high-potassium and phosphorus fertilizer (NPK 5-15-15) for taproot expansion.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Avoid fresh manure which causes root forking and splitting.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatments needed for healthy roots.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Insect mesh netting over beds to exclude carrot rust flies.

organic_remedies.org1: Companion planting with Alliums (onions/leeks) to mask the carrot scent from pests.
organic_remedies.org2: Mulch with finely shredded leaves to conserve soil moisture.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest when roots reach mature diameter for peak sweetness and crispness.

Downy_mildew.severity: Moderate to High (Rapid Spoilage in Cool, Humid Conditions)

disease_symptoms.s1: Angular, pale green to bright chlorotic yellow patches on the upper leaf surface delineated by leaf veins.
disease_symptoms.s2: Purplish-gray to brown downy felt or fungal sporulation on the corresponding underside of the leaves in humid weather.
disease_symptoms.s3: Severe infections cause rapid foliar browning, leaf curl, and premature defoliation.

disease_causes.c1: Water mold oospores and sporangia driven by extended leaf wetness (>6 hours) and high humidity (>85%).
disease_causes.c2: Temperatures between 15°C and 22°C (59°F–72°F) coupled with dense, unventilated plant spacing.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide wide plant spacing and north-south row alignment to accelerate leaf drying from morning sunlight.
disease_prevention.p2: Use drip or furrow irrigation exclusively; never apply overhead sprinklers during evening or overcast periods.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced N-P-K nutrition (10-10-10 or 8-16-16) with supplemental potassium silicate to fortify epidermal leaf cell walls.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Avoid heavy spring nitrogen applications which promote excessively soft, vulnerable succulence.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Curative systemic fungicides: Mefenoxam + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ), Cymoxanil (Curzate), or Dimethomorph (Acrobat 50WP).
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Protectant contact fungicides: Copper hydroxide (Kocide 3000) or Chlorothalonil applied every 7-10 days.

organic_remedies.org1: Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis (Serenade ASO) or Trichoderma harzianum as early preventive sprays.
organic_remedies.org2: Potassium bicarbonate (MilStop) or copper octanoate (copper soap) to suppress spore germination without synthetic residue.

disease_control.ctrl1: Scout lower canopy leaves twice weekly and immediately rogue out early infected leaves into sealed bags.
disease_control.ctrl2: Rotate out of host crop families for a minimum of 2-3 years after harvest.

disease_symptoms.s1: Lush, dark green crinkled (savoy) or smooth tender leaves with crisp turgid petiole structure.
disease_symptoms.s2: Uniform leaf blade color with no yellow chlorosis, downy sporulation, or leaf spot lesions.
disease_symptoms.s3: Compact rosette growth habit with vigorous crown and white fibrous roots.

disease_causes.c1: Cool-season growth under moist, organic-rich soil (pH 6.5–7.0) with consistent moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain consistent shallow cultivation to suppress weeds without disturbing spinach's delicate feeder roots.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure afternoon shade or shade cloth during warm spells to prevent premature bolting.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Nitrogen-rich organic foliar feeds (fish emulsion, blood meal, or compost tea) applied bi-weekly.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Light side-dressing of balanced organic 5-5-5 fertilizer during peak rosette leaf expansion.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy spinach.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Insecticidal soap or neem spray if leaf miner scouts or aphids are detected on outer leaves.

organic_remedies.org1: Apply a thin layer of compost mulch around crowns to regulate soil temperature and prevent soil splashing.
organic_remedies.org2: Companion planting with radishes, onions, and strawberries to naturally deter pests.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest outer leaves continuously (cut-and-come-again) to promote vigorous center leaf development.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, rounded globe-shaped crimson-purple taproot with smooth skin and unbroken crown.
disease_symptoms.s2: Vibrant upright green and maroon foliage free from Cercospora leaf spot or downy mildew.
disease_symptoms.s3: Crisp internal rings with deep ruby coloration and sweet, earthy flavor.

disease_causes.c1: Loose, stone-free sandy loam soil with adequate boron and neutral pH (6.0–6.8).

disease_prevention.p1: Thin beet seedlings early to 7-10 cm apart to ensure unobstructed root bulb expansion.
disease_prevention.p2: Maintain uniform soil moisture to prevent woody texture, root splitting, or internal ring discoloration.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium and phosphorus fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10 or bone meal with wood ash) to promote bulb sizing.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply trace micronutrient boron (Solubor at 1.5 g/L) if soil is boron-deficient to prevent internal black heart.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical fungicide or pesticide required for prime healthy beetroot.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Diatomaceous earth dusting around seedlings to stop flea beetles.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch beds with aged straw or shredded leaves to maintain cool root temperatures.
organic_remedies.org2: Incorporate well-rotted leaf mold compost before sowing to loosen heavy clay soil.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest roots when they reach 5–8 cm in diameter for prime tenderness and maximum nutritional value.

disease_symptoms.s1: Plump, crisp, and firm scarlet or white taproots with smooth surface and zero splitting.
disease_symptoms.s2: Healthy green lyrate lobed leaves with vibrant coloration and no flea beetle shot-hole damage.
disease_symptoms.s3: Crisp, peppery white internal flesh without pithiness or internal discoloration.

disease_causes.c1: Fast-growing cool-season conditions (21-30 days to maturity) in light, friable, moisture-retentive soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Sow successionally every 10–14 days for a continuous crisp harvest throughout spring and autumn.
disease_prevention.p2: Cover fresh beds with lightweight floating row covers immediately after seeding to exclude root maggots.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Low-nitrogen organic compost; excess nitrogen creates oversized leafy tops with diminutive, split roots.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Light application of aged wood ash or potassium sulfate to enhance root firmness.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for fast-turnaround healthy radishes.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Spinosad or pyrethrin spot-spray only if intense flea beetle infestation occurs.

organic_remedies.org1: Dust bed perimeter with wood ash or neem cake powder to deter subterranean larvae.
organic_remedies.org2: Keep soil evenly damp; drought stress triggers harsh bitterness, premature bolting, and woody pith.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest promptly when roots reach golf-ball diameter; leaving radishes in soil causes rapid pithiness.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, plump, aromatic rhizome fingers with thin, tan skin and yellow fibrous flesh.
disease_symptoms.s2: Erect, reed-like pseudostems with vibrant lanceolate green leaves free from leaf spot or bacterial wilt.
disease_symptoms.s3: Clean root buds showing vigorous sprouts with no softness, foul smell, or water-soaking.

disease_causes.c1: Rich, well-draining warm soil with high organic matter, partial canopy shade, and high humidity.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant only certified disease-free, plump seed rhizomes treated with Trichoderma viride.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure raised beds with excellent internal drainage to prevent rhizome rot (soft rot).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium organic fertilizer (NPK 8-8-16) applied in 3 split doses during active tillering.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or neem cake at 45 and 90 days after planting.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy rhizomes.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Preventive drench with Mancozeb (0.2%) or Copper Oxychloride (0.25%) before monsoon.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch generously with green leaves (10-12 tons/ha) at planting and repeated after 45 days to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
organic_remedies.org2: Soil solarization of seedbeds prior to planting to eradicate soil-borne Pythium and Ralstonia.

disease_control.ctrl1: Hill up soil around ginger pseudostems periodically to protect expanding rhizome hands from sun-greening.

disease_symptoms.s1: Angular, chlorotic yellow patches on the upper surface of spinach leaves bounded by veins.
disease_symptoms.s2: Dense purplish-gray to violet-white downy felt or sporulation on the corresponding leaf undersides in humid weather.
disease_symptoms.s3: Infected spinach leaves curl downward, pucker, become brittle, turn tan-brown, and rot quickly.

disease_causes.c1: Obligate biotrophic oomycete Peronospora effusa favored by cool, moist weather (8°C to 18°C / 46°F to 64°F).
disease_causes.c2: Prolonged free moisture or dew on spinach leaves for more than 4 hours combined with high relative humidity (>85%).
disease_causes.c3: Overhead irrigation, dense seed spacing, and lack of crop rotation in leafy green beds.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant certified downy mildew-resistant spinach varieties (races 1-19 resistant hybrids e.g. Seaside, Correnta, Bloomsdale).
disease_prevention.p2: Strictly utilize drip or sub-surface irrigation; avoid overhead watering or sprinkling leaves in late afternoon.
disease_prevention.p3: Ensure wide plant spacing (15-20 cm) and row orientation parallel to prevailing winds for rapid foliage drying.
disease_prevention.p4: Practice a minimum 3-year crop rotation away from spinach, chard, and beet family members.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced organic fertilization (NPK 8-8-8 or 5-5-5) with supplemental potassium sulfate to thicken epidermal leaf cuticles.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Avoid excessive nitrogen side-dressings, which trigger soft, highly succulent leaf growth prone to downy mildew penetration.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Foliar spray of soluble calcium and silica to fortify cellular cell walls against oomycete haustoria.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Systemic curative fungicides: Mefenoxam + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ), Oxathiapiprolin (Orondis Ultra), or Cyazofamid (Ranman 400SC).
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Protectant contact fungicides: Copper octanoate (Liquid Copper) or Chlorothalonil applied at 7-day intervals.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Fosetyl-Al (Aliette) or potassium phosphite to stimulate systemic acquired resistance throughout plant vascular tissues.

organic_remedies.org1: Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (Serenade ASO) or Trichoderma harzianum as early preventive washes.
organic_remedies.org2: Potassium Bicarbonate spray (1 tbsp per gallon of water with organic spreader-sticker soap) to inhibit spore germination.
organic_remedies.org3: Dilute raw milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water) applied in morning sunlight to lyse fungal membranes.

disease_control.ctrl1: Immediately inspect rows and rogue out diseased spinach plants in sealed trash bags; do not discard in compost piles.
disease_control.ctrl2: Sterilize harvest knives, shears, and field crates in 10% bleach or 70% ethanol between plots.
disease_control.ctrl3: Clean and disc under crop residue immediately after final harvest to bury surviving oospores deep in the soil profile.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant emerald green, deeply lobed foliage with active tendrils climbing trellises smoothly.

disease_symptoms.s3: Abundant bright yellow solitary male and female flowers opening in early morning sunlight.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide sturdy vertical trellising or overhead bower systems to keep vines and fruits off soil.
disease_prevention.p2: Drip irrigation at root zone; avoid wetting dense climbing canopy.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply farmyard manure (FYM) supplemented with NPK 6-12-12 during vine running and flowering.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Foliar application of micronutrient mixture (zinc, boron) to improve fruit set and reduce blossom drop.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy bitter gourd vines.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Pheromone fruit fly traps (cue-lure) installed at 4-6 traps per acre.

disease_control.ctrl1: Regular harvesting of tender immature green fruits every 2-3 days to encourage continuous fruiting.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium and nitrogen fertilizer (NPK 10-10-15) during early vegetative cupping stage.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for pristine healthy cabbage heads.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt kurstaki) for biological control of diamondback moth and cabbage loopers.

organic_remedies.org1: Yellow sticky cards for monitoring whiteflies and aphids.
organic_remedies.org2: Intercropping with aromatic herbs (thyme, rosemary, dill) to deter cabbage white butterflies.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest heads cleanly with a sharp knife leaving 2-3 protective wrapper leaves when firm.

disease_symptoms.s1: Dense, crisp, creamy-white curd with compact curd branching and zero ricing or bracting.
disease_symptoms.s2: Upright, waxy blue-green jacket leaves closely shielding the developing central head.
disease_symptoms.s3: Absence of downy mildew spots, black rot, or hollow stem browning.

disease_prevention.p2: Ensure uniform irrigation; avoid water stress during curd initiation.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced brassica fertilizer (NPK 12-12-17) supplemented with Boron (Borax 10 kg/ha) to prevent curd browning.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Molybdenum spray (sodium molybdate 0.05%) to prevent whiptail leaf deformity.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for prime healthy cauliflower curds.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Spinosad or neem spray if cabbage aphid colonies appear on jacket leaves.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch soil with organic straw to maintain cool root temperatures and conserve moisture.
organic_remedies.org2: Spray compost tea every 14 days to enhance systemic phyllosphere immunity.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest when heads are compact and smooth (15-20 cm diameter) before curd segments begin separating.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, multi-clove subterranean bulbs wrapped in papery white or purple outer tunics.
disease_symptoms.s2: Erect, flat, strap-like linear leaves with vibrant gray-green coloration and clean margins.
disease_symptoms.s3: Solid basal plate with vigorous white root fibrils free from white rot sclerotia or nematode galls.

disease_causes.c1: Winter vernalization followed by warm, dry bulb maturation in loose, well-draining soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant only certified clean, plump seed cloves; never plant grocery store culinary bulbs.
disease_prevention.p2: Avoid poorly drained soils to prevent basal rot (Fusarium) and white rot (Stromatinia).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-phosphorus bone meal or rock phosphate in furrow at planting time.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with nitrogen (blood meal or calcium nitrate) early spring; stop nitrogen 4 weeks before harvest.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required for healthy garlic crops.

organic_remedies.org2: Wood ash amendment to supply potassium and discourage onion thrips.

disease_control.ctrl1: Stop irrigation 2 weeks before lifting; cure harvested bulbs in well-ventilated dry shade for 3-4 weeks.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, dark green elliptical foliage with winged petioles and characteristic citrus aroma.

disease_symptoms.s3: Absence of citrus canker lesions, greasy spot, or Huanglongbing (citrus greening) mottle.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Specialized Citrus Fertilizer (NPK 13-7-13 or 8-8-8) containing chelated Zinc, Manganese, and Iron.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for prime healthy lemon trees.

organic_remedies.org1: Cold-pressed neem oil (1%) sprayed during flush growth to protect young foliage from citrus leaf miners.
organic_remedies.org2: Release beneficial ladybugs and lacewings to naturally eliminate citrus aphids.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest ripe yellow lemons with clippers flush to calyx without tearing peel tissue.

disease_symptoms.s1: Plump, firm globe-shaped bulbs with crisp, dry, paper-like golden or red outer wrapper scales.
disease_symptoms.s2: Tubular, hollow blue-green cylindrical leaves standing upright with zero purple blotch or thrips stippling.
disease_symptoms.s3: Tight, well-sealed neck tissue indicating proper maturity and excellent storage potential.

disease_causes.c1: Correct photoperiod (short-day or long-day according to latitude) in loose, rich, friable soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Avoid deep planting; onion bulbs should form right at the soil surface.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure wide row spacing (25-30 cm) and avoid overhead irrigation to prevent foliar blight.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced organic base fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10) with sulfur (gypsum or sulfate of potash) for pungency.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Side-dress with calcium nitrate at early leaf expansion; stop feeding once bulbing initiates.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for prime healthy onion bulbs.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Spinosad or blue sticky cards if onion thrips pressure rises.

organic_remedies.org1: Dust diatomaceous earth around row margins to deter onion maggots.
organic_remedies.org2: Mulch between rows with straw to prevent weed competition without burying bulb necks.

disease_control.ctrl1: When 50-70% of tops naturally fall over, bend remaining tops; cure bulbs in warm dry shade.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, narrow, lanceolate dark green leaves with reddish young petioles and spiny branch tips.
disease_symptoms.s2: Bright scarlet tubular flowers setting into firm, round, leathery crimson-crowned fruits.

disease_causes.c1: Arid to semi-arid climate with hot, dry summers and mild winters in well-draining alkaline/neutral soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune suckers and interior water shoots to maintain open center tree or multi-stem bush shape.
disease_prevention.p2: Sanitize pruning shears with 70% alcohol; avoid mechanical fruit wounding.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium fertilizer (NPK 10-10-20) during fruit enlargement stage to prevent fruit cracking.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Foliar spray of Boron (Solubor 1g/L) and Calcium chloride (5g/L) during bloom to reinforce rind elasticity.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required for healthy pomegranate trees.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Bactericidal copper oxychloride (0.25%) dormant preventative wash prior to monsoon.

organic_remedies.org1: Bag individual fruits with non-woven polypropylene bags to protect against pomegranate butterfly (anar caterpillar).
organic_remedies.org2: Apply neem cake (2 kg per mature tree) to soil around drip line.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest fruits with clippers when rinds achieve deep ruby blush and make a metallic sound when tapped.

disease_symptoms.s1: Broad, palmate, deeply lobed dark green leaves with bristly trichomes and sturdy fibrous stems.
disease_symptoms.s2: Tender, slender, 5-8 ridged green pods snapping crisply at tips with zero yellow vein clearing.
disease_symptoms.s3: Large, creamy-yellow hibiscus-like blossoms with maroon center eye flowering daily.

disease_causes.c1: Warm weather crop (25°C–35°C) thriving in full sun and fertile, loamy, moisture-retentive soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV) resistant cultivars (e.g. Parbhani Kranti, Arka Anamika).
disease_prevention.p2: Control whitefly vectors using yellow sticky traps and barrier crops (maize/sorghum border).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply composted cow manure plus NPK 10-10-10 at sowing, followed by split nitrogen top-dressings.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Supplement with potassium to support continuous pod formation over an extended 60-day picking cycle.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for prime healthy okra plants.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Neem oil (5ml/L) or botanical insecticidal soap if whitefly nymphs appear.

organic_remedies.org1: Intercrop with marigolds to deter root-knot nematodes in soil.
organic_remedies.org2: Mulch root zones with dried grass or leaves to suppress weed competition.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest tender pods daily or every other day when 7-10 cm long to maintain continuous vegetative flowering.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant, tender pinnate green leaves with curled climbing tendrils anchoring firmly to trellises.
disease_symptoms.s2: Plump, cylindrical, sweet green pods filled with tender round seeds with zero powdery mildew bloom.
disease_symptoms.s3: Clean white and pink butterfly-shaped blossoms blooming abundantly in cool spring weather.

disease_causes.c1: Cool-season growth (10°C–18°C) in well-aerated soil with active Rhizobium leguminosarum root nodulation.

disease_prevention.p1: Trellis vines to ensure airflow and rapid drying; avoid dense matting on wet soil.
disease_prevention.p2: Plant powdery mildew-resistant cultivars for late spring sowings.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Low-nitrogen, high-phosphorus organic blend (NPK 4-12-8) plus Rhizobium legume seed inoculant.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Supplement with wood ash or potassium sulfate to enhance sugar synthesis and pod sweetness.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for prime healthy garden peas.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Wettable sulfur or potassium bicarbonate only if powdery mildew threatens late season.

organic_remedies.org1: Spray compost tea bi-weekly to coat leaves with beneficial protective microflora.
organic_remedies.org2: Companion plant with carrots, radishes, and turnips.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest pods frequently when peas are round and tender before pod walls turn fibrous and starchy.

disease_symptoms.s1: Angular, chlorotic yellow patches on the upper surface of spinach leaves bounded by veins.
disease_symptoms.s2: Dense purplish-gray to violet-white downy felt or sporulation on the corresponding leaf undersides in humid weather.
disease_symptoms.s3: Infected spinach leaves curl downward, pucker, become brittle, turn tan-brown, and rot quickly.

disease_causes.c1: Obligate biotrophic oomycete Peronospora effusa favored by cool, moist weather (8°C to 18°C / 46°F to 64°F).
disease_causes.c2: Prolonged free moisture or dew on spinach leaves for more than 4 hours combined with high relative humidity (>85%).
disease_causes.c3: Overhead irrigation, dense seed spacing, and lack of crop rotation in leafy green beds.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant certified downy mildew-resistant spinach varieties (races 1-19 resistant hybrids e.g. Seaside, Correnta, Bloomsdale).
disease_prevention.p2: Strictly utilize drip or sub-surface irrigation; avoid overhead watering or sprinkling leaves in late afternoon.
disease_prevention.p3: Ensure wide plant spacing (15-20 cm) and row orientation parallel to prevailing winds for rapid foliage drying.
disease_prevention.p4: Practice a minimum 3-year crop rotation away from spinach, chard, and beet family members.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced organic fertilization (NPK 8-8-8 or 5-5-5) with supplemental potassium sulfate to thicken epidermal leaf cuticles.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Avoid excessive nitrogen side-dressings, which trigger soft, highly succulent leaf growth prone to downy mildew penetration.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Foliar spray of soluble calcium and silica to fortify cellular cell walls against oomycete haustoria.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: Systemic curative fungicides: Mefenoxam + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ), Oxathiapiprolin (Orondis Ultra), or Cyazofamid (Ranman 400SC).
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Protectant contact fungicides: Copper octanoate (Liquid Copper) or Chlorothalonil applied at 7-day intervals.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Fosetyl-Al (Aliette) or potassium phosphite to stimulate systemic acquired resistance throughout plant vascular tissues.

organic_remedies.org1: Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (Serenade ASO) or Trichoderma harzianum as early preventive washes.
organic_remedies.org2: Potassium Bicarbonate spray (1 tbsp per gallon of water with organic spreader-sticker soap) to inhibit spore germination.
organic_remedies.org3: Dilute raw milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water) applied in morning sunlight to lyse fungal membranes.

disease_control.ctrl1: Immediately inspect rows and rogue out diseased spinach plants in sealed trash bags; do not discard in compost piles.
disease_control.ctrl2: Sterilize harvest knives, shears, and field crates in 10% bleach or 70% ethanol between plots.
disease_control.ctrl3: Clean and disc under crop residue immediately after final harvest to bury surviving oospores deep in the soil profile.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant emerald green, deeply lobed foliage with active tendrils climbing trellises smoothly.
disease_symptoms.s2: Firm, warty, elongated green fruits with crisp ridged skin and zero water-soaked spots.
disease_symptoms.s3: Abundant bright yellow solitary male and female flowers opening in early morning sunlight.

disease_causes.c1: Warm tropical/subtropical climate (25°C–35°C) with well-drained sandy loam and high organic content.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide sturdy vertical trellising or overhead bower systems to keep vines and fruits off soil.
disease_prevention.p2: Drip irrigation at root zone; avoid wetting dense climbing canopy.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply farmyard manure (FYM) supplemented with NPK 6-12-12 during vine running and flowering.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Foliar application of micronutrient mixture (zinc, boron) to improve fruit set and reduce blossom drop.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy bitter gourd vines.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Pheromone fruit fly traps (cue-lure) installed at 4-6 traps per acre.

organic_remedies.org1: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) sprayed as preventive measure against sucking pests.
organic_remedies.org2: Bagging young fruits with paper bags to protect against melon fruit fly oviposition.

disease_control.ctrl1: Regular harvesting of tender immature green fruits every 2-3 days to encourage continuous fruiting.

disease_symptoms.s3: Smooth bark, sound scaffolding branches, and unblemished growing fruits.

disease_causes.c1: Good orchard management, annual pruning, and balanced soil fertility.

disease_prevention.p1: Annual dormant winter pruning to open center canopy to sunlight.

organic_remedies.org1: Apply kaolin clay (Surround WP) to protect fruit from sunburn and insect pests.

disease_control.ctrl1: Maintain clean orchard floor free of tall weeds and fallen debris.

Arracha___healthy.name: Arracha (Arracacia xanthorrhiza)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Arracha.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Beet_fodder_mangel___healthy.name: Beet, fodder (mangel) (Beta vulgaris)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Beet, fodder (mangel).
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Cassava_manioc___healthy.name: Cassava (manioc) (Manihot esculenta)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Cassava (manioc).
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Celery___healthy.name: Celery (Apium graveolens)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Celery.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.

Chicory_for_greens___healthy.name: Chicory for greens (Cichorium intybus)
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Chicory for greens.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.

Cocoyam___healthy.name: Cocoyam (Colocasia esculenta)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Cocoyam.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.

fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.

Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, uniform dark green cylindrical fruits with crisp texture and fresh bloom.
disease_symptoms.s2: Broad triangular leaves with vibrant chlorophyll and zero powdery or downy mildew patches.
disease_symptoms.s3: Active climbing tendrils and plentiful bright yellow blossoms with strong bee pollination.

disease_causes.c1: Consistent deep watering, full sunshine, and fertile organic soil enriched with compost.

disease_prevention.p1: Grow on vertical trellises or A-frames to keep foliage dry and promote rapid air circulation.
disease_prevention.p2: Drip irrigate at the base; avoid overhead sprinkling that triggers downy mildew.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium organic fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10) with seaweed meal for trace minerals.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with vermicompost when flowering begins.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical fungicides necessary for healthy cucurbits.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Preventative copper or sulfur spray only if persistent humid rain occurs.

organic_remedies.org1: Milk spray dilution (40% milk / 60% water) weekly to create a protective bio-film against mildews.
organic_remedies.org2: Encourage pollinator bees by planting dill and borage nearby.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest cucumbers regularly when crisp and tender to stimulate continued floral production.

Dasheen___healthy.name: Dasheen (Colocasia esculenta)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Dasheen.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Endive___healthy.name: Endive (Cichorium endivia)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Endive.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Garlic_dry___healthy.name: Garlic, dry (Allium sativum)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Garlic, dry.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Ginger_Adrak___healthy.name: Ginger / Adrak (Zingiber officinale)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Ginger / Adrak.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

sources: All Vegetables (NZ Māori & Global Botanical Index)
Koppert India & ICAR Plant Protection Standards

Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Gourd_Lagenaria_spp___healthy.name: Gourd Lagenaria spp; (Cucurbita spp.)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Gourd Lagenaria spp;.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant lobed green canopy, vigorous tendrils, and uniform grape clusters.
disease_symptoms.s2: Leaf margins show clean cellular integrity.
disease_symptoms.s3: Vigorous shoot and root growth.

disease_causes.c1: Balanced environmental conditions.
disease_causes.c2: Optimum cultural management.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide adequate plant spacing to allow continuous air circulation.
disease_prevention.p2: Water at the soil level using drip irrigation; keep leaves dry.
disease_prevention.p3: Practice strict 3-year crop rotation and sanitize pruning equipment with 70% alcohol.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply balanced NPK formulation suitable for Grape (e.g. NPK 10-10-10 or 5-10-15).
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Supplement with Potassium and Calcium to reinforce plant cell walls against infection.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers that generate soft, vulnerable tissue.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: None needed.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Dormant copper sprays in winter to eliminate overwintering spores.

organic_remedies.org1: Cold-pressed Neem Oil spray (1% concentration) applied every 7 days.
organic_remedies.org2: Bio-fungicides based on Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride.
organic_remedies.org3: Potassium Bicarbonate foliar wash (1 tbsp per gallon water) to suppress sporulation.

disease_control.ctrl1: Continue regular maintenance and weeding.
disease_control.ctrl2: Inspect crops weekly for early detection of pest and fungal hotspots.

Grass_orchard___healthy.name: Grass, orchard (Dactylis glomerata)
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Grass, orchard.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

Horseradish___healthy.name: Horseradish (Armoracia rusticana)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Horseradish.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.
