Jerusalem_artichoke___healthy.name: Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Jerusalem artichoke.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, dark green elliptical foliage with winged petioles and characteristic citrus aroma.
disease_symptoms.s2: Clean, smooth-skinned lemon fruit with bright yellow peel, firm pulp, and high acidity.
disease_symptoms.s3: Absence of citrus canker lesions, greasy spot, or Huanglongbing (citrus greening) mottle.

disease_causes.c1: Subtropical to Mediterranean climate with full sun exposure (>8 hours) and well-drained acidic/neutral soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune interior criss-crossing water shoots to allow continuous sunlight penetration throughout canopy.
disease_prevention.p2: Paint trunk bases with white dilute latex paint to prevent sunscald and borer entry.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Specialized Citrus Fertilizer (NPK 13-7-13 or 8-8-8) containing chelated Zinc, Manganese, and Iron.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Foliar application of Epsom salts (Magnesium Sulfate 15g/L) twice yearly to prevent leaf yellowing.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for prime healthy lemon trees.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Dormant horticultural oil spray to smother citrus leaf miner and scale insect crawlers.

organic_remedies.org1: Cold-pressed neem oil (1%) sprayed during flush growth to protect young foliage from citrus leaf miners.
organic_remedies.org2: Release beneficial ladybugs and lacewings to naturally eliminate citrus aphids.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest ripe yellow lemons with clippers flush to calyx without tearing peel tissue.

Mangel_fodder_beet___healthy.name: Mangel (fodder beet) (Beta vulgaris)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Mangel (fodder beet).
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Melon_except_watermelon___healthy.name: Melon (except watermelon) (Cucumis melo)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Melon (except watermelon).
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Parsnip___healthy.name: Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Parsnip.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Long lance-shaped vibrant green leaves and clean velvet peach fruits.
disease_symptoms.s2: Leaf margins show clean cellular integrity.
disease_symptoms.s3: Vigorous shoot and root growth.

disease_causes.c1: Balanced environmental conditions.
disease_causes.c2: Optimum cultural management.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide adequate plant spacing to allow continuous air circulation.
disease_prevention.p2: Water at the soil level using drip irrigation; keep leaves dry.
disease_prevention.p3: Practice strict 3-year crop rotation and sanitize pruning equipment with 70% alcohol.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply balanced NPK formulation suitable for Peach (e.g. NPK 10-10-10 or 5-10-15).
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Supplement with Potassium and Calcium to reinforce plant cell walls against infection.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers that generate soft, vulnerable tissue.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: None needed.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Dormant copper sprays in winter to eliminate overwintering spores.

organic_remedies.org1: Cold-pressed Neem Oil spray (1% concentration) applied every 7 days.
organic_remedies.org2: Bio-fungicides based on Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride.
organic_remedies.org3: Potassium Bicarbonate foliar wash (1 tbsp per gallon water) to suppress sporulation.

disease_control.ctrl1: Continue regular maintenance and weeding.
disease_control.ctrl2: Inspect crops weekly for early detection of pest and fungal hotspots.

Observe proper pre-harvest intervals (PHI) and rotation of chemical modes of action.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, narrow, lanceolate dark green leaves with reddish young petioles and spiny branch tips.
disease_symptoms.s2: Bright scarlet tubular flowers setting into firm, round, leathery crimson-crowned fruits.
disease_symptoms.s3: Clean bark and rind free from bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oily spots) or fruit borer entry holes.

disease_causes.c1: Arid to semi-arid climate with hot, dry summers and mild winters in well-draining alkaline/neutral soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Prune suckers and interior water shoots to maintain open center tree or multi-stem bush shape.
disease_prevention.p2: Sanitize pruning shears with 70% alcohol; avoid mechanical fruit wounding.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium fertilizer (NPK 10-10-20) during fruit enlargement stage to prevent fruit cracking.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Foliar spray of Boron (Solubor 1g/L) and Calcium chloride (5g/L) during bloom to reinforce rind elasticity.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required for healthy pomegranate trees.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Bactericidal copper oxychloride (0.25%) dormant preventative wash prior to monsoon.

organic_remedies.org1: Bag individual fruits with non-woven polypropylene bags to protect against pomegranate butterfly (anar caterpillar).
organic_remedies.org2: Apply neem cake (2 kg per mature tree) to soil around drip line.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest fruits with clippers when rinds achieve deep ruby blush and make a metallic sound when tapped.

disease_symptoms.s1: Lush, dark green, upright compound leaves with robust stems.
disease_symptoms.s2: White, pink, or purple flowers blossoming uniformly across rows.
disease_symptoms.s3: Clean subterranean stolons with smooth, firm, unblemished tubers.

disease_causes.c1: Cool weather, well-drained acidic soil (pH 5.5 - 6.5), and adequate moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Hill plants with loose soil and straw as vines grow.
disease_prevention.p2: Inspect leaf undersides weekly for Colorado potato beetle egg clusters or early blight spots.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: NPK 10-15-15 fertilizer supplemented with Bone meal and greensand at hilling stage.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Maintain consistent soil moisture during tuber initiation and bulking.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical applications needed.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch deeply with straw to deter potato beetles and prevent tuber greening.

disease_control.ctrl1: Keep tubers well covered with soil to protect against greening and sun scald.

Potato_sweet___healthy.name: Potato, sweet (Ipomoea batatas)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Potato, sweet.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Red_beet___healthy.name: Red beet (Beta vulgaris)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Red beet.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Rhubarb___healthy.name: Rhubarb (Rheum spp.)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Rhubarb.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Glossy, deep green, uniformly colored foliage with clean serrated margins.
disease_symptoms.s2: Sturdy, erect canes with healthy pith and firm green bark.
disease_symptoms.s3: Well-formed flower buds with clean sepals and vibrant blossom development.
disease_symptoms.s4: Zero spotting, powdery residues, rust pustules, or insect webbing.

disease_causes.c1: Proper cultural care: adequate sunlight, balanced soil nutrition, and optimal irrigation.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain 6-8 hours of direct sunlight and 3-foot spacing.
disease_prevention.p2: Inspect leaf undersides weekly for early detection of aphids, spider mites, or black spot.
disease_prevention.p3: Sanitize pruners between bushes using rubbing alcohol.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply slow-release balanced rose food (NPK 10-10-10 or 8-12-8) every 4-6 weeks during blooming season.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Add 1 cup of alfalfa meal and 1 tbsp of Epsom salt (Magnesium Sulfate) around the drip line in spring.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Cease nitrogen fertilizing 6 weeks before first anticipated frost to harden off canes.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical pesticides required for healthy roses.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Optional preventative botanical dormant spray (horticultural oil) in late winter.

organic_remedies.org1: Beneficial companion planting with Alliums (garlic/chives) and Marigolds to deter aphids and nematodes.
organic_remedies.org2: Compost tea foliar drench monthly to sustain healthy phyllosphere microflora.

disease_control.ctrl1: Continue regular deadheading of spent blooms to channel energy into vigorous root and shoot systems.

Salsify___healthy.name: Salsify (Tragopogon porrifolius)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Salsify.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Trifoliate clean green leaves with sturdy pods and active nitrogen-fixing nodules.

disease_causes.c1: Balanced environmental conditions.

disease_symptoms.s1: Lush, dark green crinkled (savoy) or smooth tender leaves with crisp turgid petiole structure.
disease_symptoms.s2: Uniform leaf blade color with no yellow chlorosis, downy sporulation, or leaf spot lesions.
disease_symptoms.s3: Compact rosette growth habit with vigorous crown and white fibrous roots.

disease_causes.c1: Cool-season growth under moist, organic-rich soil (pH 6.5–7.0) with consistent moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain consistent shallow cultivation to suppress weeds without disturbing spinach's delicate feeder roots.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure afternoon shade or shade cloth during warm spells to prevent premature bolting.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Nitrogen-rich organic foliar feeds (fish emulsion, blood meal, or compost tea) applied bi-weekly.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Light side-dressing of balanced organic 5-5-5 fertilizer during peak rosette leaf expansion.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for healthy spinach.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Insecticidal soap or neem spray if leaf miner scouts or aphids are detected on outer leaves.

organic_remedies.org1: Apply a thin layer of compost mulch around crowns to regulate soil temperature and prevent soil splashing.
organic_remedies.org2: Companion planting with radishes, onions, and strawberries to naturally deter pests.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest outer leaves continuously (cut-and-come-again) to promote vigorous center leaf development.

Sugar_beet___healthy.name: Sugar beet (Beta vulgaris)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Sugar beet.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Sweet_Potato_Kumara___healthy.name: Sweet Potato / Kumara (Ipomoea batatas)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Sweet Potato / Kumara.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

sources: All Vegetables (NZ Māori & Global Botanical Index)

Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant deep green foliage with uniform chlorophyll distribution across all leaves.
disease_symptoms.s2: Stems are thick, sturdy, and covered with healthy trichome glandular hairs.
disease_symptoms.s3: Abundant bright yellow blossoms with successful fruit set and smooth skin.
disease_symptoms.s4: Zero spots, chlorosis, curling, greasy lesions, or pest damage.

disease_causes.c1: Optimal environmental balance: 6-8 hours of direct sun, consistent watering, and fertile soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain 2-3 inches of organic straw or wood mulch under plants.
disease_prevention.p2: Prune suckers and lowest leaves touching the ground to prevent soil-borne fungal spores.
disease_prevention.p3: Water deeply at ground level using drip emitters; keep leaves dry.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced Tomato Food (NPK 4-18-38 or 5-10-10) with Calcium, Magnesium, and Sulfur.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Side-dress with bone meal and compost when fruit first sets to provide slow-release Phosphorus.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Maintain soil pH between 6.2 and 6.8 for optimal nutrient uptake.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatments necessary for healthy plants.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Optional preventative biological drench with mycorrhizal fungi at root zone.

organic_remedies.org1: Companion planting with Basil and French Marigolds to naturally repel hornworms and aphids.
organic_remedies.org2: Compost tea foliar spray to maintain robust beneficial microbial colonies.

disease_control.ctrl1: Support heavy vines with sturdy cages or trellising to prevent fruit contact with soil.

Watermelon___healthy.name: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus)
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Watermelon.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Air potato.

Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Beet___healthy.name: Beet (Botanical classification per World Crops Database (world-crops.com))
Beet___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per World Crops Database (world-crops.com)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Beet.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, rounded globe-shaped crimson-purple taproot with smooth skin and unbroken crown.
disease_symptoms.s2: Vibrant upright green and maroon foliage free from Cercospora leaf spot or downy mildew.
disease_symptoms.s3: Crisp internal rings with deep ruby coloration and sweet, earthy flavor.

disease_causes.c1: Loose, stone-free sandy loam soil with adequate boron and neutral pH (6.0–6.8).

disease_prevention.p1: Thin beet seedlings early to 7-10 cm apart to ensure unobstructed root bulb expansion.
disease_prevention.p2: Maintain uniform soil moisture to prevent woody texture, root splitting, or internal ring discoloration.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium and phosphorus fertilizer (NPK 5-10-10 or bone meal with wood ash) to promote bulb sizing.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply trace micronutrient boron (Solubor at 1.5 g/L) if soil is boron-deficient to prevent internal black heart.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical fungicide or pesticide required for prime healthy beetroot.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Diatomaceous earth dusting around seedlings to stop flea beetles.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch beds with aged straw or shredded leaves to maintain cool root temperatures.
organic_remedies.org2: Incorporate well-rotted leaf mold compost before sowing to loosen heavy clay soil.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest roots when they reach 5–8 cm in diameter for prime tenderness and maximum nutritional value.

bitter_gourd_bitter_melon.condition: Healthy Bitter Gourd / Bitter Melon Specimen
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Bitter Gourd / Bitter Melon.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

sources: All Vegetables (NZ Māori & Global Botanical Index)

Black_radish___healthy.name: Black radish (Botanical classification per World Crops Database (world-crops.com))
Black_radish___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per World Crops Database (world-crops.com)
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Black radish.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Broccoli___healthy.name: Broccoli (Brassica oleracea var. italica)
symptoms: Vigorous vegetative growth and species-typical morphology for prime Broccoli.
Healthy foliar color, robust stems, and optimal reproductive flowering/fruiting vigor.
Specimen shows strong cellular defense with zero necrotic spots or pathogen lesions.
causes: Favorable climate with balanced sunlight, temperature, and moisture conditions.
Fertile, well-aerated soil structure with appropriate nutrient availability.
Adequate agronomic care following integrated pest and nutrient management principles.
prevention: Select certified disease-resistant crop cultivars and clean planting material.
Maintain clean cultivation, weed eradication, and field sanitation.
Monitor crop fields twice weekly for early detection of pests or physiological stress.
fertilizer: Soil-test-based balanced NPK application supplemented with well-rotted organic manure.
Balanced micronutrient cocktail (Zinc, Iron, Manganese, Boron) via foliar application.
Humic and fulvic acid soil drenches to optimize root nutrient absorption capacity.
organic: Koppert biological control solutions tailored to pest and pathogen pressure.
Trichoderma and Pseudomonas bio-inoculants for root zone health and systemic acquired resistance.
Botanical neem oil formulations (1500 - 10000 ppm) for preventive insect control.
pesticides: Integrate biorational biopesticides and target-specific registered crop protection agents.
Observe proper pre-harvest intervals (PHI) and rotation of chemical modes of action.

sources: All Vegetables (NZ Māori & Global Botanical Index)

disease_symptoms.s1: Tight, firm, dense spherical heads surrounded by broad, waxy outer wrapper leaves.
disease_symptoms.s2: Uniform bluish-green or reddish-purple leaf coloration free from black rot V-shaped lesions.
disease_symptoms.s3: Sturdy central stalk and healthy taproot system with no clubroot swelling.

disease_causes.c1: Cool-season conditions (15°C–20°C) with abundant organic matter and steady moisture.

disease_prevention.p1: Maintain soil pH around 6.5–7.2 to naturally suppress Plasmodiophora brassicae (clubroot).
disease_prevention.p2: Practice strict 4-year crop rotation with non-brassica crops (solanaceous, legumes, cucurbits).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-potassium and nitrogen fertilizer (NPK 10-10-15) during early vegetative cupping stage.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Apply calcium nitrate to prevent internal tipburn (calcium deficiency in inner leaves).

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No synthetic chemical intervention required for pristine healthy cabbage heads.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt kurstaki) for biological control of diamondback moth and cabbage loopers.

organic_remedies.org1: Yellow sticky cards for monitoring whiteflies and aphids.
organic_remedies.org2: Intercropping with aromatic herbs (thyme, rosemary, dill) to deter cabbage white butterflies.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest heads cleanly with a sharp knife leaving 2-3 protective wrapper leaves when firm.

symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Cassava.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.

Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.

Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.

Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.

Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.

disease_symptoms.s1: Dense, crisp, creamy-white curd with compact curd branching and zero ricing or bracting.
disease_symptoms.s2: Upright, waxy blue-green jacket leaves closely shielding the developing central head.
disease_symptoms.s3: Absence of downy mildew spots, black rot, or hollow stem browning.

disease_causes.c1: Cool daytime temperatures (16°C–22°C) with high organic fertility and uninterrupted watering.

disease_prevention.p1: Tie outer wrapper leaves over curd (blanching) when head reaches 5 cm diameter to protect pure white color.
disease_prevention.p2: Ensure uniform irrigation; avoid water stress during curd initiation.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Balanced brassica fertilizer (NPK 12-12-17) supplemented with Boron (Borax 10 kg/ha) to prevent curd browning.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Molybdenum spray (sodium molybdate 0.05%) to prevent whiptail leaf deformity.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical intervention needed for prime healthy cauliflower curds.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Spinosad or neem spray if cabbage aphid colonies appear on jacket leaves.

organic_remedies.org1: Mulch soil with organic straw to maintain cool root temperatures and conserve moisture.
organic_remedies.org2: Spray compost tea every 14 days to enhance systemic phyllosphere immunity.

disease_control.ctrl1: Harvest when heads are compact and smooth (15-20 cm diameter) before curd segments begin separating.

symptoms: Vigorous vegetative growth and species-typical morphology for prime Ancho Pepper.
Healthy foliar color, robust stems, and optimal reproductive flowering/fruiting vigor.
Specimen shows strong cellular defense with zero necrotic spots or pathogen lesions.
causes: Favorable climate with balanced sunlight, temperature, and moisture conditions.
Fertile, well-aerated soil structure with appropriate nutrient availability.
Adequate agronomic care following integrated pest and nutrient management principles.
prevention: Select certified disease-resistant crop cultivars and clean planting material.
Maintain clean cultivation, weed eradication, and field sanitation.
Monitor crop fields twice weekly for early detection of pests or physiological stress.
fertilizer: Soil-test-based balanced NPK application supplemented with well-rotted organic manure.
Balanced micronutrient cocktail (Zinc, Iron, Manganese, Boron) via foliar application.
Humic and fulvic acid soil drenches to optimize root nutrient absorption capacity.
organic: Koppert biological control solutions tailored to pest and pathogen pressure.
Trichoderma and Pseudomonas bio-inoculants for root zone health and systemic acquired resistance.
Botanical neem oil formulations (1500 - 10000 ppm) for preventive insect control.
pesticides: Integrate biorational biopesticides and target-specific registered crop protection agents.
Observe proper pre-harvest intervals (PHI) and rotation of chemical modes of action.

Angelica___healthy.name: Angelica (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Angelica___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Angelica.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

Arikara_Squash___healthy.name: Arikara Squash (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Arikara_Squash___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Arikara Squash.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Asian Greens.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

Baby_Boo_Pumpkin___healthy.name: Baby Boo Pumpkin (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Baby_Boo_Pumpkin___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Baby Boo Pumpkin.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Bamboo_Shoot___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vigorous vegetative growth and species-typical morphology for prime Bamboo Shoot.
Healthy foliar color, robust stems, and optimal reproductive flowering/fruiting vigor.
Specimen shows strong cellular defense with zero necrotic spots or pathogen lesions.
causes: Favorable climate with balanced sunlight, temperature, and moisture conditions.
Fertile, well-aerated soil structure with appropriate nutrient availability.
Adequate agronomic care following integrated pest and nutrient management principles.
prevention: Select certified disease-resistant crop cultivars and clean planting material.
Maintain clean cultivation, weed eradication, and field sanitation.
Monitor crop fields twice weekly for early detection of pests or physiological stress.
fertilizer: Soil-test-based balanced NPK application supplemented with well-rotted organic manure.

organic: Koppert biological control solutions tailored to pest and pathogen pressure.

Botanical neem oil formulations (1500 - 10000 ppm) for preventive insect control.
pesticides: Integrate biorational biopesticides and target-specific registered crop protection agents.
Observe proper pre-harvest intervals (PHI) and rotation of chemical modes of action.

Baobab_Leaves___healthy.name: Baobab Leaves (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)

symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Baobab Leaves.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.

organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.

Bintje_Potato___healthy.name: Bintje Potato (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Bintje_Potato___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Bintje Potato.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Bitter_Melon___healthy.name: Bitter Melon (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Bitter_Melon___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Bitter Melon.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Black_Eyed_Susan_Vine___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Black-Eyed Susan Vine.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.

Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.

organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.

Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Chioggia_Beet___healthy.name: Chioggia Beet (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Chioggia_Beet___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Robust root development, uniform taper, and healthy dermal skin typical of prime Chioggia Beet.
Foliar crown shows vigorous vegetative petiole growth without stunting, yellowing, or leaf curl.
Subterranean storage tissue free from nematode galling, wireworm tunnels, or bacterial soft rot.
causes: Deep, loose, stone-free friable soil allowing unrestricted taproot and tuber expansion.
Optimum soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 with adequate potassium reserves.
Consistent moisture regime preventing root cracking, splitting, or hollow heart.
prevention: Deep plowing (30 cm) and ridge or raised bed planting to enhance drainage and aeration.
Long crop rotation cycle with alliums and cereals to break root-knot nematode cycles.
Solarization of nursery beds and certified disease-free seed tubers or certified seed stock.
fertilizer: NPK 5-10-15 or 6-12-18 emphasizing potassium and phosphorus for storage organ enlargement.
Avoid excessive nitrogen which causes excessive top growth and split, hairy roots.
Boron (Solubor 1 g/L) application at root bulking to prevent internal black heart or browning.
organic: Koppert Larvanem (Heterorhabditis bacteriophora) against root grubs, wireworms, and root maggots.
Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum) for suppression of Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium rots.
Trichoderma viride bio-fertilizer enriched in vermicompost applied at sowing/planting.
pesticides: Biorational Bacillus thuringiensis for cutworms and soil application of Metarhizium anisopliae.
Fluopyram or bio-nematicides for root-knot nematode suppression.

Chive___healthy.name: Chive (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Chive___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Erect, tubular cylindrical foliage with healthy blue-green waxy cuticular bloom in Chive.
Firm bulb development with tight, dry outer scales and well-anchored root system.
Zero lesions, purple blotch, tip dieback, or basal plate rot.
causes: Sufficient photoperiod (short-day or long-day) triggering bulb swelling.
Cool early vegetative phase (13-24°C) followed by warmer ripening conditions (25-35°C).
Loose, fertile soil with pH 6.0-7.0 and excellent drainage.
prevention: Avoid deep transplanting; set seedlings or cloves at recommended 2-3 cm depth.
Withhold irrigation 10-14 days before harvest to allow neck closure and scale curing.
Implement 4-year crop rotation excluding other allium crops.
fertilizer: NPK 8-15-15 basal application with sulfur (30 kg/ha elemental S) to enhance pungency and bulb quality.
Top-dress with urea or ammonium sulfate before bulb initiation; cease N at bulking.
Zinc sulfate (2 g/L) spray at 30 and 45 days after planting.
organic: Koppert Thripex (Neoseiulus cucumeris) for predatory control of onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).
Pseudomonas fluorescens seed and bulb treatment against damping off and basal rot.
Verticillium lecanii (Lecanicillium) bio-insecticide for thrips nymph control.
pesticides: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L) for purple blotch and Stemphylium blight control.
Spinetoram or Spinosad for thrips suppression under heavy pressure.

disease_symptoms.s1: Vibrant wide arching green leaves with sturdy stalks and full silk development.
disease_symptoms.s2: Leaf margins show clean cellular integrity.
disease_symptoms.s3: Vigorous shoot and root growth.

disease_causes.c1: Balanced environmental conditions.
disease_causes.c2: Optimum cultural management.

disease_prevention.p1: Provide adequate plant spacing to allow continuous air circulation.
disease_prevention.p2: Water at the soil level using drip irrigation; keep leaves dry.
disease_prevention.p3: Practice strict 3-year crop rotation and sanitize pruning equipment with 70% alcohol.

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: Apply balanced NPK formulation suitable for Corn (Maize) (e.g. NPK 10-10-10 or 5-10-15).
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Supplement with Potassium and Calcium to reinforce plant cell walls against infection.
fertilizer_recommendation.f3: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers that generate soft, vulnerable tissue.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: None needed.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf3: Dormant copper sprays in winter to eliminate overwintering spores.

organic_remedies.org1: Cold-pressed Neem Oil spray (1% concentration) applied every 7 days.
organic_remedies.org2: Bio-fungicides based on Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride.
organic_remedies.org3: Potassium Bicarbonate foliar wash (1 tbsp per gallon water) to suppress sporulation.

disease_control.ctrl1: Continue regular maintenance and weeding.
disease_control.ctrl2: Inspect crops weekly for early detection of pest and fungal hotspots.

Egyptian_Onion___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Erect, tubular cylindrical foliage with healthy blue-green waxy cuticular bloom in Egyptian Onion.
Firm bulb development with tight, dry outer scales and well-anchored root system.
Zero lesions, purple blotch, tip dieback, or basal plate rot.
causes: Sufficient photoperiod (short-day or long-day) triggering bulb swelling.
Cool early vegetative phase (13-24°C) followed by warmer ripening conditions (25-35°C).
Loose, fertile soil with pH 6.0-7.0 and excellent drainage.
prevention: Avoid deep transplanting; set seedlings or cloves at recommended 2-3 cm depth.
Withhold irrigation 10-14 days before harvest to allow neck closure and scale curing.
Implement 4-year crop rotation excluding other allium crops.
fertilizer: NPK 8-15-15 basal application with sulfur (30 kg/ha elemental S) to enhance pungency and bulb quality.
Top-dress with urea or ammonium sulfate before bulb initiation; cease N at bulking.
Zinc sulfate (2 g/L) spray at 30 and 45 days after planting.
organic: Koppert Thripex (Neoseiulus cucumeris) for predatory control of onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).
Pseudomonas fluorescens seed and bulb treatment against damping off and basal rot.
Verticillium lecanii (Lecanicillium) bio-insecticide for thrips nymph control.
pesticides: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L) for purple blotch and Stemphylium blight control.
Spinetoram or Spinosad for thrips suppression under heavy pressure.

Ensete___healthy.name: Ensete (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Ensete___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Ensete.

Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

Fenugreek_Methi___healthy.name: Fenugreek / Methi (Trigonella foenum-graecum)
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Fenugreek / Methi.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

sources: All Vegetables (NZ Māori & Global Botanical Index)

Field_Cucumber___healthy.name: Field Cucumber (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Field_Cucumber___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vigorous vine elongation, healthy palmate foliage, and prolific flowering in Field Cucumber.
Uniform fruit set without blossom-end decay, fruit fly oviposition marks, or mosaic mottling.
Deep green leaves with zero powdery mildew superficial white powder on adaxial surfaces.
causes: Warm growing season with temperatures between 24°C and 32°C and high solar irradiance.
Well-drained sandy loam soil enriched with matured farmyard manure (FYM).
Optimal pollination assisted by beneficial honeybees and bumblebees.
prevention: Trellising and vertical staking systems to keep vines and fruit elevated above wet soil.
Pheromone cue-lure traps (10-12 traps/acre) for fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) suppression.
Drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage and prevent powdery and downy mildew outbreaks.
fertilizer: NPK 10-26-26 or 12-32-16 at basal stage followed by soluble potassium nitrate during fruit sizing.
Calcium chelate foliar spray during flowering to avert blossom-end rot.
Magnesium sulfate (5 g/L) to maintain vigorous photosynthesis in large vine canopies.
organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.

Flat_Italian_Onion___healthy.name: Flat Italian Onion (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Flat_Italian_Onion___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Erect, tubular cylindrical foliage with healthy blue-green waxy cuticular bloom in Flat Italian Onion.
Firm bulb development with tight, dry outer scales and well-anchored root system.
Zero lesions, purple blotch, tip dieback, or basal plate rot.
causes: Sufficient photoperiod (short-day or long-day) triggering bulb swelling.
Cool early vegetative phase (13-24°C) followed by warmer ripening conditions (25-35°C).
Loose, fertile soil with pH 6.0-7.0 and excellent drainage.
prevention: Avoid deep transplanting; set seedlings or cloves at recommended 2-3 cm depth.
Withhold irrigation 10-14 days before harvest to allow neck closure and scale curing.
Implement 4-year crop rotation excluding other allium crops.
fertilizer: NPK 8-15-15 basal application with sulfur (30 kg/ha elemental S) to enhance pungency and bulb quality.
Top-dress with urea or ammonium sulfate before bulb initiation; cease N at bulking.
Zinc sulfate (2 g/L) spray at 30 and 45 days after planting.
organic: Koppert Thripex (Neoseiulus cucumeris) for predatory control of onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).
Pseudomonas fluorescens seed and bulb treatment against damping off and basal rot.
Verticillium lecanii (Lecanicillium) bio-insecticide for thrips nymph control.
pesticides: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L) for purple blotch and Stemphylium blight control.
Spinetoram or Spinosad for thrips suppression under heavy pressure.

French_Sorrel___healthy.name: French Sorrel (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
French_Sorrel___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy French Sorrel.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

disease_symptoms.s1: Firm, multi-clove subterranean bulbs wrapped in papery white or purple outer tunics.
disease_symptoms.s2: Erect, flat, strap-like linear leaves with vibrant gray-green coloration and clean margins.
disease_symptoms.s3: Solid basal plate with vigorous white root fibrils free from white rot sclerotia or nematode galls.

disease_causes.c1: Winter vernalization followed by warm, dry bulb maturation in loose, well-draining soil.

disease_prevention.p1: Plant only certified clean, plump seed cloves; never plant grocery store culinary bulbs.
disease_prevention.p2: Avoid poorly drained soils to prevent basal rot (Fusarium) and white rot (Stromatinia).

fertilizer_recommendation.f1: High-phosphorus bone meal or rock phosphate in furrow at planting time.
fertilizer_recommendation.f2: Top-dress with nitrogen (blood meal or calcium nitrate) early spring; stop nitrogen 4 weeks before harvest.

pesticides_and_fungicides.pf1: No chemical treatment required for healthy garlic crops.
pesticides_and_fungicides.pf2: Trichoderma seed clove dip (10g/L) prior to autumn sowing.

organic_remedies.org1: Thick winter straw mulch (10-15 cm) to suppress frost heave and conserve spring soil moisture.
organic_remedies.org2: Wood ash amendment to supply potassium and discourage onion thrips.

disease_control.ctrl1: Stop irrigation 2 weeks before lifting; cure harvested bulbs in well-ventilated dry shade for 3-4 weeks.

Green_Onion___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Erect, tubular cylindrical foliage with healthy blue-green waxy cuticular bloom in Green Onion.
Firm bulb development with tight, dry outer scales and well-anchored root system.
Zero lesions, purple blotch, tip dieback, or basal plate rot.
causes: Sufficient photoperiod (short-day or long-day) triggering bulb swelling.
Cool early vegetative phase (13-24°C) followed by warmer ripening conditions (25-35°C).
Loose, fertile soil with pH 6.0-7.0 and excellent drainage.
prevention: Avoid deep transplanting; set seedlings or cloves at recommended 2-3 cm depth.
Withhold irrigation 10-14 days before harvest to allow neck closure and scale curing.
Implement 4-year crop rotation excluding other allium crops.
fertilizer: NPK 8-15-15 basal application with sulfur (30 kg/ha elemental S) to enhance pungency and bulb quality.
Top-dress with urea or ammonium sulfate before bulb initiation; cease N at bulking.
Zinc sulfate (2 g/L) spray at 30 and 45 days after planting.
organic: Koppert Thripex (Neoseiulus cucumeris) for predatory control of onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).
Pseudomonas fluorescens seed and bulb treatment against damping off and basal rot.
Verticillium lecanii (Lecanicillium) bio-insecticide for thrips nymph control.
pesticides: Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole (1 ml/L) for purple blotch and Stemphylium blight control.
Spinetoram or Spinosad for thrips suppression under heavy pressure.

Green_Seaweed___healthy.name: Green Seaweed (Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia)
Green_Seaweed___healthy.pathogen: Botanical classification per GoodGoodGood Vegetable Encyclopedia
symptoms: Vibrant, turgid foliage with optimal chlorophyll density characteristic of healthy Green Seaweed.
Uniform green lamina with clear epidermal venation and zero signs of chlorotic spotting or downy mildew sporulation.
Petiole and stem tissues demonstrate high cell turgor and resilience against foliar lodging.
causes: Optimum temperature range between 15°C and 22°C with adequate cool root-zone moisture.
Balanced soil pH of 6.2 - 7.0 with well-drained, organic-rich sandy loam.
Good air circulation between plant canopies minimizing relative humidity buildup.
prevention: Maintain morning drip irrigation to ensure foliage dries thoroughly before nightfall.
Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-chenopod and non-brassica crops.
Ensure plant spacing of 20-30 cm to allow sunlight penetration and canopy ventilation.
fertilizer: NPK 10-10-10 or 8-4-8 balanced baseline fertilizer supplemented with compost tea.
Foliar spray of Seaweed extract (2 ml/L) for micronutrient supplementation (Iron, Magnesium, Manganese).
Calcium nitrate (1 g/L) side-dressing during vegetative expansion to prevent tip-burn.
organic: Koppert Trianum-P (Trichoderma harzianum strain T-22) for root shield and soil-borne protection.
Bacillus subtilis biological preventive spray against downy mildew and leaf blight.
Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% EC at 3 ml/L) against aphids, thrips, and leaf miners.
pesticides: Potassium silicate or Copper oxychloride (2 g/L) as a protective botanical fungicide if humidity exceeds 85%.
Spinosad biorational formulation for caterpillar and leaf miner management.

organic: Koppert Swirski-Mite (Amblyseius swirskii) against thrips, whiteflies, and spider mites.
Koppert Spical (Neoseiulus californicus) for biological spider mite management.
Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide against powdery mildew.
pesticides: Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) spray against early sap-sucking pests.
Sulfur-based wettable fungicide (2 g/L) or Copper hydroxide for foliar disease management.
